title: add-lightweight-rag-toolchain-stitcher-and-playground
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding teams iterate on mix-and-match retrieval+tooling patterns but often copy/paste glue code across repos. This PR adds a compact 'toolchain stitcher' example and a paired playground to demonstrate wiring multiple tool adapters (HTTP webhooks, DB lookups, schema-validated tool contracts) into an offline-first RAG session. The artifact set is intentionally small and opinionated: a TypeScript playground micro-app (browser + local dev server), a Go microservice tool-adapter (lightweight stub for simulated external APIs), an authoring README with step-by-step quickstart, and a docs site fragment that explains the pattern and telemetry knobs.

What this PR contains (high level):
- examples/rag-toolchain-stitcher/: new example workspace with an opinionated layout (src/, adapters/, fixtures/, telemetry/).
- examples/rag-toolchain-stitcher/playground-ts/: minimal React+Vite runner with local mock index and tool bindings; supports stepwise replay and deterministic seeds for e2e tests.
- examples/rag-toolchain-stitcher/tool-adapters/go-stub/: tiny Go HTTP adapter that demonstrates authenticated tool calls, backoff retry examples, and contract validation using JSON Schema.
- docs/snippets/rag-toolchain-patterns.md: short doc snippet intended for inclusion in the docs site; explains when to use stitcher pattern vs monolithic tool adapters.
- test/fixtures/*: authored prompts and small corpus used by CI smoke tests.

Checklist (manual & automated):
- [x] core quickstart README with start/stop and example commands
- [x] playground TS dev server + instructions
- [x] Go adapter with Dockerfile for Private deployment testing
- [x] unit-level smoke tests (sync e2e using local dev server)
- [x] telemetry probes (compact; opt-in via env VAR) and sample metrics emitted
- [x] docs snippet and architecture diagram (ASCII) included
- [x] license headers and CLA sign-off by author

Why unique: This PR focuses on the 'stitcher' design — a small runtime that composes independent tool adapters at runtime via a typed contract, rather than coupling tools into a single orchestrator. It surfaces practical tradeoffs: caching boundary placement, auth propagation, request routing by policy, and replay determinism for authoring/eval. The playground emphasizes reproducible authoring (seeded runs & step replay) so teams can write regression tests for prompt/tool interactions.

Risks & mitigations: The Go adapter is intentionally non-production (no DB). I added explicit README warnings and an example Docker Compose service that runs the adapter behind a simulated gateway. Telemetry is opt-in and disabled by default. The sample keys are ephemeral and documented.
